name: security-boundary
instructions: The Lambda is the public entry point. Slack request signatures must be verified before any work, with a timestamp window against replay; the rate limiter must hold per user and per channel; nothing from the request may reach a shell, a query or a log unescaped.

name: model-and-secrets
instructions: API keys and tokens come only from the environment or Secrets Manager and never reach a log, a Slack message or a tool result. The model ID and endpoint must stay OpenRouter's (provider/model). Any env passed to the SDK or to MCP subprocesses must not widen what secrets those processes see.

name: agent-tools
instructions: The agent acts for Slack users. Tool allowlists must stay narrow; the URL fetcher must refuse private, link-local and metadata addresses and follow redirects only within the allowlist; Drive and GitHub writes must stay within the documented scopes. A prompt-injected document must not be able to widen what the agent can do.

name: admin-commands
instructions: Admin commands change behaviour for everyone; check who may run each one and that the check happens before any change is stored. Slack replies must not echo secrets or other users' private data.

name: migrations
instructions: Schema changes must be backward compatible with the agent and Lambda versions still running during a deploy: add before you use, never rename or drop in the same release. Generated drizzle files must match the schema source.

name: deploy
instructions: Deploy and CI changes: secrets referenced must exist, permissions stay minimal, and a dev deploy must not be able to touch prod.
